name: faremeter

memo.one_liner: Open-source TypeScript framework (client library, middleware, facilitator, gateway, wallet integrations) that lets AI agents and other software make blockchain payments over HTTP 402, supporting x402 and MPP on Solana and EVM, sponsored by ABK Labs.
memo.thesis_fit: Direct fit: it is infrastructure for agents paying per request over HTTP 402 (x402 v1/v2, MPP), with wallet and chain-agnostic plugins on both Solana and EVM. The sources show developer adoption signals but no evidence of paid or transacting usage.

claims.text: Faremeter describes itself as a framework for agents and other utilities to transparently make machine payments using web infrastructure.
claims.quote: A universal framework designed to allow agents and other utilities to transparently make machine payments using web infrastructure.

claims.text: The approach is built on HTTP 402 Payment Required with a standard-, wallet- and blockchain-agnostic plugin system.
claims.quote: Using HTTP and the existing `402 Payment Required` concepts.

claims.text: It supports both v1 and v2 of Coinbase's x402, negotiated automatically.
claims.quote: both v1 and v2 of the protocol, negotiated automatically.

claims.text: It ships the MPP charge intent on Solana, while noting the MPP spec is still evolving.
claims.quote: the spec is still evolving; we currently ship the `charge` intent on Solana.

claims.text: AP2, Cloudflare Pay-Per-Crawl and L402 are tracked for future support but not yet shipped.
claims.quote: We're tracking these for future support:

claims.text: EVM support covers gasless USDC via EIP-3009 on networks including Base, Polygon, Monad and Skale.
claims.quote: EVM `exact` over EIP-3009 gasless USDC in [@faremeter/payment-evm](./packages/payment-evm), with network coverage including Base, Polygon, Monad, and Skale

claims.text: The main repo has 25 forks, a sign of developer interest but not of payment volume.
Commits across the owner's top 5 repos were 1180 in the last 90 days, versus 1156 in the prior 90 days, so velocity is sustained and flat.
Total commits across those repos stand at 3635 since the org was created in 2025.
The project is sponsored and built by ABK Labs engineers along with open-source contributors.
claims.quote: Faremeter is sponsored and built by the engineers at [ABK Labs](https://abklabs.com) along with other open-source contributors.

claims.text: Faremeter ranks 4 among all sourced candidates in the GitHub-only screening model.
There is no Hacker News presence: 0 stories with the company name in the title.

pmf.rationale: Forks and stars [c7] show real developer interest, and the framework covers wallets, chains and standards, but the sources show no customers, transaction volume or pricing evidence. That puts it at the developer-adoption tier, not the paying tier.

narrative.rationale: The story is a clear wedge on HTTP 402 and x402/MPP [c2][c3][c4], with a path to a platform via the facilitator, gateway and wallet plugins. Standards are still moving [c4][c5], and the sources do not state a commercial model or an edge over Coinbase's own x402 tooling. ABK Labs sponsorship [c10] leaves the company/product relationship unclear.

execution.rationale: Commit velocity is high and steady [c8][c9], and the team has shipped x402 v2, MPP charge and multiple EVM chains [c3][c4][c6]. The sources do not show contributor counts, so the multi-person claim is unverified, and the commit totals cover the top 5 repos, not only the main framework.

risks: Commercial model unclear: it is an open-source sponsored project of ABK Labs, with no pricing, customers or revenue shown, so a venture-scale business is unproven.
Standards risk: MPP is still evolving and x402 is controlled by Coinbase, which could absorb or commoditize the facilitator, middleware and client layers.
No evidence of transacting usage: forks and stars are the only adoption signals, with no volume, customers or production deployments cited.
Entity and dependency risk: the project is built by ABK Labs engineers, so it is unclear whether Faremeter is a separate fundable entity, who owns the IP, and how much team time is dedicated to it.
open_questions: Is Faremeter a standalone company or an ABK Labs project, and who owns the IP and would take the investment?
Who is using it in production, and what are the transaction counts or volume through Faremeter facilitators or gateways?
What is the business model: hosted facilitator fees, managed gateway, enterprise support, or something else?
How many distinct people commit regularly, and how many are not ABK Labs employees?
How does Faremeter differentiate from Coinbase's x402 reference SDKs and other facilitators, and what happens if MPP and x402 converge?
Which of the 1180 recent commits are in the core framework versus the other 15 repos?

pmf.rationale: Forks indicate interest [c7], but their independence, active use and integration depth are unknown. The provided sources do not establish outside production adoption or transacting usage, so the developer-adoption tier is not yet convincingly demonstrated.

narrative.rationale: The HTTP payment middleware wedge and extensible architecture are clear and directly relevant to agent commerce [c1; d_d7f80babf38c9414]. Standards support strengthens the product story [c3][c4], but commercial differentiation and the path to a defensible platform remain hypotheses.

execution.rationale: Owner-level activity and documented protocol support suggest shipping capacity [c8][c3][c4][c6]. However, the main repository's last-push metadata creates an unresolved tension with recent owner-level activity [d_748e85e901fac822]; core-product velocity, contributor breadth and response speed to standards changes are unverified.

unsupported_claims.reason: The attached quote supports the HTTP payment mechanism but does not substantiate the plugin system or its standard, wallet and blockchain independence. Those properties appear elsewhere in the document and need their own supporting span.
The quote does not identify the named standards. Future-support tracking also does not independently establish that no partial implementation has shipped.

The attached metric supports only recent commit volume. The comparison requires gh.commits_prev_90d, while the repository scope and observation windows require additional provenance; one metric receipt does not support every number in the text.

The total-commit metric does not establish organization creation timing or that all counted commits occurred after organization creation. Repository history can predate its current owner, and the receipt does not support the year in the text.
The metric measures stories with the company name in the title, not all Hacker News presence. It cannot rule out comments, differently titled submissions or other mentions.

missing_risks: Core-product maintenance risk: reconcile the main repository's last-push metadata with recent owner-level activity before treating aggregate commits as evidence of current framework development.
Adoption-quality risk: establish whether forks represent independent users, maintained integrations or inactive copies.
Payment-security diligence is absent: ask about audits, signing permissions, key custody, replay protection and failed-payment handling.
Compatibility and operational reliability remain unverified: ask for integration tests and production evidence supporting the documented standards and network coverage.
critique.strongest_counterargument: The strongest case against advancing is that owner-level development activity and documented capabilities do not yet establish independent demand or sustained maintenance of the investable product. Advancement should depend on resolving core-repository activity and obtaining credible outside production-use evidence.

disagreements: critic flags 5 claim(s) as unsupported by their quote
